title: Who is doing what (checked 11 October 2026)
summary: The institutions, programmes and results that define quantum oncology in 2026 — Cleveland Clinic and IBM, Wellcome Leap's Q4Bio and its prize, biomarker and neoantigen projects — against the state of the hardware.

shots.kicker: Unit 8 · The field in 2026 · checked 11 Oct 2026
shots.title:
Who is doing
what.
shots.subtitle: Demonstrations, estimates and plans — kept apart.
shots.narration: This lesson is a dated snapshot — the check date is on the title card. The field moves quickly, so the habit to learn is separating demonstrations from estimates and plans.

The milestones: a quantum computer installed at Cleveland Clinic in 2023; Wellcome Leap's Q4Bio programme the same year; the KRAS study in 2025; a photosensitizer resource estimate that December; the Q4Bio prize in April 2026; and a neoantigen project launched this month.

shots.text: March 2023: an IBM Quantum System One at **Cleveland Clinic** — described as the first dedicated to healthcare research.
shots.narration: In March 2023 Cleveland Clinic and IBM unveiled an on-site IBM Quantum System One, described as the first quantum computer dedicated to healthcare research, inside a ten-year partnership. That is a fact about deployment, not about results.

shots.text: Q4Bio prizes: **$2M** for a working application on **>50 qubits** at depth **10³–10⁴**; **$5M** for quantum **advantage**.
shots.narration: Wellcome Leap's Q4Bio set two bars: two million dollars for a working application on more than fifty qubits at a program depth of a thousand to ten thousand, and five million for quantum advantage over the best classical methods.

shots.label: in the prize-winning photodynamic-therapy workflow
shots.context: Algorithmiq with IBM and Cleveland Clinic · April 2026 · no grand-prize winner announced
shots.narration: In April 2026 the Algorithmiq-led team, with IBM and Cleveland Clinic, met the two-million-dollar criteria, computing excited-state properties of a photodynamic-therapy drug on circuits of up to a hundred qubits. No grand-prize winner for advantage was announced.

shots.text: Six finalists — Infleqtion, Nottingham, Harvard, Stanford, Algorithmiq, Oxford; **five of six** used IBM hardware.
shots.narration: The six finalists were led by Infleqtion, the University of Nottingham, Harvard, Stanford, Algorithmiq and Oxford, and five of the six ran on IBM hardware.

shots.text: Cancer biomarkers: quantum **feature selection** on real hardware, forecasting **head-and-neck** treatment response — claimed gains **not yet peer-reviewed**.
shots.narration: On the oncology side, Infleqtion, the University of Chicago and MIT took quantum feature selection for cancer biomarkers onto real hardware, aiming to forecast treatment response in head-and-neck cancer. Their claimed improvement is, so far, a press-release quotation.

shots.text: October 2026: a NEDO project (to **March 2029**) will use AI plus quantum optimisation to design **neoantigen** cancer-vaccine candidates.
shots.narration: And in October 2026, NEC, Taiho Pharmaceutical, the Japanese Foundation for Cancer Research, AIST and Waseda University announced a project running to March 2029 to design neoantigen cancer-vaccine candidates with AI and quantum optimisation. A plan, not a result.

shots.text: Error correction is real: **below threshold** (Google, 2024); **48** logical qubits on **98** physical (Quantinuum, 2025).
shots.narration: The hardware is moving. Google showed error correction below threshold in 2024, and Quantinuum's Helios ran forty-eight error-corrected logical qubits on ninety-eight physical ones in 2025.

shots.text: Roadmap: **~200 logical qubits by 2029** (IBM, an estimate). The P450 estimate needs **millions** of physical qubits.
shots.narration: IBM's roadmap targets about two hundred logical qubits by 2029 — a plan, not a fact. Compare the needs: photosensitizer screening at a hundred and eighty to three hundred and fifty logical qubits, the largest P450 model at millions of physical qubits.

shots.text: Advantage claims draw **classical replies**: IBM's 2023 utility run and 2026 advantage run were both simulated classically soon after.
shots.narration: And advantage claims draw classical replies. IBM's 2023 utility experiment was reproduced by tensor networks, and its 2026 seventy-qubit advantage claim was simulated classically within weeks, in a preprint. Expect the same for any biomedical claim.

right.heading: Not yet
items: Quantum advantage on any oncology task
Peer-reviewed biomarker gains from quantum hardware

shots.narration: The scoreboard, as of today. Demonstrated: hundred-qubit workflows on real biomedical problems, error correction below threshold, and quantum-assisted molecules made and tested. Not yet: advantage on any oncology task, peer-reviewed biomarker gains, or any benefit to a patient.

steps.title: Demonstrated, estimated or contested?
steps.brief: Sort these 2026-landscape statements by their evidence level.

cards.text: A ~100-qubit workflow computed excited-state properties of a photodynamic-therapy drug
Google's Willow showed logical errors falling as the code grew
Two quantum-assisted KRAS molecules showed activity in assays
The largest P450 model needs ~4.6 million physical qubits
IBM will have ~200 logical qubits by 2029
AI plus quantum optimisation will design neoantigen candidates by 2029
A hybrid quantum approach found novel cancer biomarkers
cards.why: A press-release quotation without peer-reviewed results when checked.

cards.text: IBM's 70-logical-qubit run is beyond classical computers
cards.why: Reproduced classically within weeks, in a preprint.

questions.prompt: What did the Q4Bio $2M prize require?
options: A working application on more than 50 qubits at program depth 10³–10⁴, with a path to scale
questions.explain: Advantage was the separate $5M grand prize; no winner was announced for it.

questions.prompt: Which statement about quantum oncology in 2026 is supported?
options: Quantum computers have improved cancer patients' outcomes
Hybrid workflows have run at ~100 qubits on biomedical problems, without demonstrated advantage
questions.explain: Demonstrations, not advantage — and no patient benefit yet.

questions.prompt: IBM's ~200-logical-qubit target for 2029 is best classified as…
questions.explain: A roadmap is a plan; treat it as an estimate until delivered.

steps.title: Homework 16 · Keep the map current
steps.brief: About 45 minutes. Landscape knowledge goes stale; build the habit of re-checking.
